# Coverage and experiment map

Every original lesson is assigned to a main textbook chapter. This maps concepts and working examples; it does not assert every subsection of each external primer is reproduced.

| Textbook chapter | Original lessons | Companion | Main worked relationship |
|---:|---|---|---|
| [01](chapters/01-coordinates.md) | 01: Tensors, Python, and the meaning of a shape; 02: Linear algebra for representations and projections | Coordinates and projections | Change an input coordinate and inspect each contribution to a learned linear map. |
| [02](chapters/02-gradients.md) | 03: Derivatives, Jacobians, and the chain rule; 06: Neural networks, backpropagation, and optimization | Gradient microscope | Compare an exact chain-rule derivative with a central difference and a descent step. |
| [03](chapters/03-probability.md) | 04: Probability, conditioning, and statistical estimation; 05: Entropy, KL divergence, softmax, and cross-entropy; 07: Language modeling from counts to autoregression | Probability and information | Inspect softmax, entropy, target loss, and logit gradients. |
| [04](chapters/04-representations.md) | 08: Tokenization, byte pairs, and text boundaries; 09: Embeddings, distributional learning, and similarity; 10: Recurrent networks, sequence-to-sequence, and alignment | Tokens and representations | Execute character byte-pair merges and retrieve a supplied embedding row. |
| [05](chapters/05-attention.md) | 11: Attention as differentiable weighted retrieval; 12: Queries, keys, values, and scaled dot-product attention; 13: Backpropagating through attention by hand | Attention workbench | Follow scores, normalization, weighted values, and a readout derivative. |
| [06](chapters/06-transformer-blocks.md) | 14: Causal masks, padding, packed sequences, and batches; 15: Multi-head, multi-query, and grouped-query attention; 16: Position, sinusoidal features, relative biases, and RoPE; 17: Residual streams, normalization, and feed-forward blocks | Masks, position, and heads | Inspect causal visibility, rotary position, and grouped head sharing. |
| [07](chapters/07-train-a-transformer.md) | 18: Encoders, decoders, and cross-attention objectives; 19: Build a complete tiny GPT from tensor operations; 20: Train, validate, checkpoint, and sample a tiny language model | Train a conditional language table | Run real gradient descent on a small next-token model; full transformer code is supplied in Python. |
| [08](chapters/08-efficient-execution.md) | 21: Pretraining data, scaling, distributed execution, and memory; 22: Decoding, temperature, KV caches, and serving; 23: Exact online attention, sparse patterns, and linear alternatives; 24: Long-context modeling and position extrapolation | Inference and context costs | Calculate cache memory, dense attention size, temperature, and cache equality. |
| [09](chapters/09-adaptation.md) | 25: Evaluation, calibration, and mechanistic investigation; 26: Instruction tuning and supervised response losses; 27: Parameter-efficient tuning, adapters, and LoRA derivatives; 28: Quantization, numerical error, and QLoRA | Adapters and precision | Compare LoRA factor paths, merged weights, and uniform quantization. |
| [10](chapters/10-experts-and-teachers.md) | 29: Mixture-of-experts routing, capacity, and balancing; 30: Knowledge distillation, temperature, and prefix distributions | Experts and teachers | Inspect router assignments, capacity overflow, and a distillation gradient. |
| [11](chapters/11-bellman-reasoning.md) | 31: Bandits, policies, returns, and Markov decision processes; 32: Bellman equations, policy evaluation, and dynamic programming; 33: Temporal differences, Q-learning, and exploration | Bellman laboratory | Compare iterated policy values with a linear solve and a residual bound. |
| [12](chapters/12-policy-gradients.md) | 34: Policy gradients and REINFORCE from the likelihood ratio; 35: Actor-critic learning and generalized advantage estimation; 36: PPO, importance ratios, clipping, and KL monitoring | Policy updates | Inspect an exact bandit gradient, GAE, and both PPO clipping signs. |
| [13](chapters/13-alignment.md) | 37: Reward modeling, RLHF, and constrained policy optimization; 38: DPO and the derivation from rewards to policy ratios; 39: GRPO, group baselines, and verifiable rewards | Preferences and alignment | Compute reference-adjusted DPO loss and group-normalized rewards. |
| [14](chapters/14-retrieval-and-context.md) | 40: Prompting, structured output, search, and test-time computation; 41: Context engineering, persistent memory, and information budgets; 42: Dense retrieval, contrastive encoders, and vector search; 43: RAG ingestion, BM25, hybrid fusion, and reranking; 44: Advanced RAG, graph retrieval, and failure diagnosis | Retrieval and context | Execute BM25, reciprocal rank fusion, and exhaustive budget selection. |
| [15](chapters/15-reliable-loops.md) | 45: Tools, bounded agent loops, graphs, and external state; 50: Recursive improvement, self-training, self-play, and evidence | Loops and improvement | Execute a bounded local loop and expose noisy winner selection. |
| [16](chapters/16-measurement.md) | 46: LLM judges, ranking, agreement, and controlled experiments; 54: Read papers, reproduce claims, and design the next experiment | Judges and evidence | Compare raw agreement, kappa, Brier loss, and simulated position bias. |
| [17](chapters/17-vision-and-recurrence.md) | 47: Vision transformers, image patches, and CLIP; 48: Generative vision-language models and cross-modal fusion; 49: Recurrent depth, recursive transformers, and latent computation | Vision and recurrence | Extract real numeric patches, calculate contrastive loss, and iterate shared state. |
| [18](chapters/18-actions-and-synthesis.md) | 51: Physical AI, partial observability, imitation, and control; 52: Action diffusion, flow matching, and learned world models; 53: Capstone: train, adapt, retrieve, and verify one local system | Actions and feedback | Simulate feedback stability and action reconstruction with explicit oracle noise. |
